text:
Simon Holmstrom has turned into a different player for the Islanders this season, and the role came first. He is playing 18:16 a night, up from 16:44, and he is now on the ice for 46% of the team's power-play chances after 19% last season. Eighteen points in 25 games, a 0.72 a game pace against 0.52 a year ago, and a seven-game point streak that ran into late November.

Some of it is real. His own chances are up to 0.88 expected goals per 60 minutes (expected goals measure the quality of the looks he gets) from 0.66, and he still carries the puck in on 57% of his entries, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season. Some of it is not. Ten goals on 6.7 expected means he is shooting 24%, and our talent range puts his true rate closer to 16%. He has also gone four games without a point.

Newsday reported the Islanders want him shooting more, and he has 41 shots in 25 games. With extension talk around him, that volume is the thing to watch once the finishing cools.
